description: Standing instructions that hold for every request: role, constraints, output format. Stable across calls, so it can be versioned and cached.
Who the model acts as and for whom: domain, audience and tone, stated in the system message.
Rules that hold for every request, such as allowed labels or things never to do. Positive and specific rules work better than vague prohibitions.
Input/output pairs placed before the real request, usually as user and assistant turns. The model copies their format, length and tone.
Markers such as `<input>` tags that separate data from instructions. They only work when the data cannot close them, so the same tag inside the data is neutralized.
Asking the model to reason step by step before answering. Reasoning models do it on their own with hidden reasoning tokens.
Prompts assembled by string concatenation across the codebase, with no single builder, no validation and no versioning.
